relevance_note: Case report of a boy with LAD-1 and an ITGB2 variant: "Next-generation sequencing established the diagnosis of LAD-1 with a mutation of ITGB2 (IVS13c.1877+1G<A)."
method_note: Index patient (case report, label 'patient') extracted by hand from the text. Table I (13 previously published LAD-1 patients with PG-like lesions) has no label column, so rows are labelled 'Table I row k', k counting data rows from the top after the two header lines (the Markdown repeats the merged header row). A script in my scratch directory transcribed Table I cells (sex, therapy, outcome, reference, CRP 'Normal', swab results) and built row-prefix spans; I checked its output against the table. Table I 'Age (y)' is age at presentation of the cutaneous manifestation per the table note, so it is recorded as onset of the PG-like lesions, not as individual onset. Reference column: rows 3-5 have empty reference cells (rows 2-5 may all be from ref 10, but the cells are empty), so source_reference_in_review is 'not reported' for them. No ITGB2 variants are printed for Table I patients; the Discussion's 'IVS10+4A>G' in a series of 4 patients from ref 10 is not tied to specific table rows, so no variant rows were created for them. Numeric neutrophil counts, numeric CRP values and CD18 % in Table I are not interpreted as leukocytosis/elevated CRP because no reference ranges or labels are given; only CRP 'Normal' is recorded as excluded elevated CRP (D-27). Positive swab cultures are recorded as phenotypic features but not mapped to the skin-infection checklist item. Index patient: variant zygosity, inheritance and pathogenicity class are not stated (parents are consanguineous; 'has not been described previously' is novelty, not a classification). 'No previous cutaneous or extracutaneous infections' refers to history before presentation. Age at death not stated (died 1 year after HSCT at age 14). No stacked cells; no contradictions found.

treatment_summary.value: oral antibiotics (cefuroxime and clindamycin); itraconazole; oral methylprednisolone without significant improvement; ustekinumab (45 mg subcutaneously) with improvement of the skin ulcers; resection of large parts of the small intestine and cecum after failed recanalization of celiac trunk stenosis; human stem cell transplantation (HSCT) at age 14 years
span: He was initially treated with oral antibiotics (cefuroxime and clindamycin)

In the absence of clinical improvement after 7 days of itraconazole therapy, a course of oral methylprednisolone was initiated (initial dose, 2 mg/kg body weight per day over 3 days, followed by tapering over 13 days), but without significant improvement.
Ustekinumab led to continuous improvement of the skin ulcers

Attempts at interventional recanalization via balloon dilatation and venous bypass failed, leading to acute intestinal ischemia and subsequent resection of large parts of the small intestine and cecum.
he underwent human stem cell transplantation (HSCT) (at age 14 years)
